reason: The cited evidence shows that a one-pot solvothermal synthesis produced PtPdCoCuNi HEA nanoparticles with isolated Pt/Pd sites and enhanced catalytic performance (E2, E3), and a model suggests limited mobility promotes mixing (E1). However, none of the cited passages directly compare low-temperature vs. high-temperature synthesis, quantify the effect of ligand/reducing agent control, or demonstrate that high-temperature annealing causes segregation and activity loss, leaving key premises about the controlled comparison unsupported.
premises: Low-temperature synthesis with controlled ligand/reducing agent yields uniform atomic mixing in PtPdCoCuNi HEA nanoparticles
Uniform mixing creates isolated Pt and Pd active sites
Isolated Pt/Pd sites enhance charge transfer and catalytic performance for nitrobenzene hydrogenation
High-temperature annealing (300–400 °C) causes phase segregation and loss of isolated sites
Kinetic limitation is the dominant factor for reliable HEA formation and performance
